name: Cut Pine Stump (Scots Pine)
description: A freshly felled Scots pine stump: low bark cylinder with tapered root flare, exposed growth rings on the cut face, and a soil-disturbance disc at the base. barkDark root → barkPine trunk → woodMid/woodDark concentric rings on top.

parts.name: Disturbed-soil / moss ground disc
parts.note: r=360 mm, h=18 mm; centre at y=0.007 → bottom at y=−0.002 (within −0.02 floor tolerance); top at y=0.016. Widest part — sets footprint w/d. tone lo = dark pressed earth.

parts.name: Root flare — wider tapered base zone
parts.note: r=310 mm at base, r2=250 mm at top (taper to trunk radius); centre at y=0.04 → bottom at y=−0.01, top at y=0.09. Dark bark at soil contact. No z-fight: bottom at −0.01 ≠ soil_base bottom −0.002 ≠ stump_body bottom 0.

parts.name: Main stump trunk cylinder — orange-brown Scots pine bark
parts.note: r=250 mm (dossier#trunk_r_mm), h=350 mm (dossier#stump_h_mm); centre at y=0.175 → bottom at y=0.00, top at y=0.35. Lower Scots pine bark: orange-brown scaly plates.

parts.name: Exposed sapwood — cut top face
parts.note: r=250 mm, h=8 mm (dossier#cut_face_th_mm); centre at y=0.354 → bottom at y=0.350 = stump_body top (opposite-normal contact, no z-fight), top at y=0.358. Pale exposed sapwood. tone hi = freshly cut lighter face.

parts.name: Growth ring band 1 — latewood (darker)
parts.note: r=175 mm (70% of trunk_r); stacked on cut_face: bottom at y=0.358 = cut_face top (opposite-normal, safe), top at y=0.366. Darker latewood annular band.

parts.name: Growth ring band 2 — earlywood (lighter)
parts.note: r=100 mm (40% of trunk_r); stacked on ring_1: bottom at y=0.366, top at y=0.374. Lighter earlywood band.

parts.name: Heartwood centre — dark core
parts.note: r=50 mm (20% of trunk_r); stacked on ring_2: bottom at y=0.374, top at y=0.382. Dense dark heartwood core reads as a knot at centre. Sets spec height max.

needs: Sourced stump height (mm) for a felled Scots pine — no quantified standard in research; 350 mm (dossier#stump_h_mm) is a design estimate
Sourced root flare radius (mm) for Pinus sylvestris at soil level — 310 mm / 124% of trunk radius (dossier#root_flare_r_mm) is a design estimate
Sourced visible root-flare height above soil (mm) — 100 mm (dossier#root_flare_h_mm) is a design estimate
